title: St John's wort infusion for mild low mood
subtitle: A traditional nervine infusion
excerpt: A hot infusion of dried St John's wort flowers and buds, made at 1-2 teaspoons per cup. Traditionally taken for mild, temporary low mood in western European herbal practice. This herb carries serious drug interactions and is not appropriate for anyone on prescription medication without consulting their prescriber first.

glossaryTerms.definition: A hot-water preparation of leaves or flowers, steeped covered to retain the volatile oils.
A herb traditionally associated with supporting the nervous system, used for tension, low mood, or mild anxiety.

content.text: St John's wort infusion is a hot-water preparation of dried aerial parts, flowers and buds, steeped covered for ten minutes. Traditionally used in western European herbal practice for mild, temporary low mood and the low spirits that can accompany a change of season. Each cup yields one dose; the standard course runs up to six weeks.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. For ongoing or serious symptoms, see a herbalist or doctor. St John's wort lowers the blood level of many prescribed drugs. Do not use if you take any of the following without speaking to your prescriber first: SSRIs or SNRIs (risk of serotonin syndrome), hormonal contraceptives (contraceptive failure risk), warfarin or other anticoagulants, transplant immunosuppressants, HIV antiretrovirals, or anti-cancer drugs. If you take any prescribed medication, speak to your prescriber before using this herb. At high doses, avoid prolonged sun exposure (photosensitising effect in fair-skinned readers). Do not use in pregnancy without guidance. Children under twelve need herbalist or paediatric guidance before using any herbal preparation.

content.text: Ingredients
Method
Bring fresh cold water to the boil, then set it aside for one minute so it drops just off the boil.
Place 1-2 teaspoons of dried St John's wort flowers and buds in a teapot or a cup fitted with a tea infuser. Use 1 teaspoon for a mild cup; 2 teaspoons for a stronger preparation.
Pour 200 ml of just-off-boil water over the herb. Cover the cup or teapot immediately to keep the aromatic oils in.
Steep for 10 minutes, covered. The water should turn a warm yellow-orange.
Strain into a cup and drink warm.
Dosing

One cup (1-2 teaspoons of dried herb per 200 ml), up to three times a day. Take for up to six weeks. If there is no improvement after four weeks, or if mood worsens, stop and consult a doctor. Do not extend the course beyond six weeks without guidance from a qualified herbalist or doctor.
Storage
Dried herb stores for up to 12 months in a sealed tin or dark glass jar, kept away from light and moisture. Prepare each cup fresh; the
infusion
should not be stored once made.
When not to use this remedy
Do not use this remedy if you are on any prescription medication without first consulting your prescriber. The drug interactions are numerous and potentially serious (see the safety notes above).

This remedy is for mild, temporary low mood only. See a GP for low mood lasting more than two weeks, low mood with hopelessness, loss of interest in everything, sleep or appetite changes, or any thoughts of self-harm or suicide. Herbal remedies are an adjunct to professional support, not a substitute. St John's wort is a
nervine
herb, not a clinical antidepressant.
Avoid prolonged sun exposure at high doses (two or more cups a day consistently), particularly if you have fair skin.
